q-82194.name: Question 2
q-82194.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 3\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}7 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & \sqrt{3} \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}|
$$
q-82194.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- The matrix $A$ has identical columns: 

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 1 \\ -7 & 1 & -1 & -7 \\ 3 & 0 & \sqrt{3} & 3\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|A|=0.$

- The matrix $B$ has a zero row: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}0 & -2 & 0.5 \\ 3 & -3 & \sqrt{5} \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- Since $C$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain 

$$
|C|=7\cdot (-1)\cdot (-2)=14\ne 0.
$$

Therefore, only $|A|$ and $|B|$ are equal to $0.$

q-82286.name: Question 3
q-82286.problem:
Which of the following determinants are equal to $0?$

$$
|A|=|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{3} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}|,\,|B|=|\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}|,\,|C|=|\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2\end{aligned}|
$$
q-82286.worked_solution:
Let's examine each of the given determinants in turn.

- Since $A$ is a diagonal matrix, we obtain 

$$
|A|=(-1)\cdot \sqrt{3}\cdot 1=-\sqrt{3}\ne 0.
$$

- The matrix $B$ has two identical rows: 

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 2 \\ 1 & -2 & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 1 & \sqrt{2}\end{aligned}]
$$

As a result, $|B|=0.$

- Since $C$ is a triangular matrix, we obtain 

$$
|C|=4\cdot (-1)\cdot 2=-8\ne 0.
$$

Therefore, only $|B|$ is equal to $0.$

q-82287.name: Question 4
q-82287.worked_solution:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

- Since $A$ has proportional rows, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 4 \\ \sqrt{3} & -1 & 1.5 \\ 3 & -9 & 12\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,det(A)=0.
$$

- For the matrix $B,$ we have

$$
det(B)=2\cdot 3-\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{3}=3.
$$

Therefore, $5det(A)+2det(B)=5\cdot 0+2\cdot 3=6.$

q-140044.name: Question 5
q-140044.worked_solution:
Let's examine each matrix in turn.

- Since $A$ has two identical columns, we obtain

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -2 & 2 & 2 \\ -1 & 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 3 & -3 & -3 & 3\end{aligned}]\,⟹\,det(A)=0.

$$

Therefore, $det(A)-3det(B)=0-3\cdot 0=0.$
